blindSummary: The only state/province in the country to have enacted a statutory bathroom restriction, and the site of a nationally significant precedent. A January 2026 law requires every educational institution in this state/province — basic, fundamental, secondary, technical and higher — to provide bathrooms separately by sex, banning shared or unisex installation and use, with fines of up to 10,000 units of local currency; a second law approved 22 December 2025 extends the ban to state/province and municipal public administration bodies; a third, tabled October 2025, would restrict school and locker-room use to the sex recorded on the birth certificate — continued legislative escalation rather than a one-off. The case that set the national precedent arose here: a trans woman was refused entry to the women's bathroom by staff at a shopping centre in the state/province's largest city, urinated on herself in front of shoppers and had to take public transport home; on 6 June 2024 the national high court rejected her appeal, leaving refusals lawful under ordinary private-premises rules. In the other direction, the state/province's largest city has a visible LGBTQ tourism scene with pride events and legal infrastructure accustomed to processing same-sex marriages and marker changes; nationwide legal rights are identical, so visitors see the same federal protections as elsewhere. Caveat: government-violence statistics sit atop the country's leading lethality figures overall, so they partly reflect general reporting levels as well as gender-specific exposure.
blindSourceSummaries: Encyclopedia overview of LGBT rights in this country: the 2011 stable-union ruling by the national high court; nationwide same-sex marriage via a 2013 national council of justice resolution (binding on all civil registry offices); the June 2019 supreme-court decision making homophobia and transphobia punishable under the anti-racism statute (imprisonment 1-5 years plus loss of public office); and gender-marker changes by self-determination.

An international LGBT-rights organisation country profile (updated 2026): over 3,000 openly LGBTQ candidates ran in the 2024 municipal elections; gender markers changeable by self-determination and trans voters may register with their lived identity; a national intersex human-rights working group installed in December 2023 with recommendations published October 2025; the national LGBTI+ health technical committee reinstated September 2025; a superior court ruling letting nonbinary people amend civil registry; and a proposed national LGBTQIA+ rights policy running alongside a conservative legislative surge in congress.

LGBTQ+ law-firm guide for expatriates considering relocation to this country: legal framework overview — the 2011 stable-union ruling, a 2013 national council of justice resolution, and the 2019 ruling treating homophobia and transphobia as crimes equivalent to racism (1-5 years plus loss of public office), plus property, inheritance and immigration treatment of same-sex spouses; major cities, including the state/province's largest city, are broadly welcoming with pride events and established legal infrastructure, smaller towns may show more social friction though legal rights are identical nationwide.
blindLocalsOnly: School-bathroom rules, birth-certificate marker procedures and employment provisions are resident-facing; a visitor never enrols or works here.
blindOutOfScope: General violent-crime exposure in this state/province mirrors the country's nationally leading lethality and is a risk to any resident or visitor regardless of gender identity; it does not move trans-specific risk.
